clue.text: The skin game ?

parts.note: a game in which players stake their clothes and shed them as they lose, ending up in their skin

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like a swindle or a tanner's trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skin game' is slang for a swindle, which is the false trail; here it is a card game where losing hands cost garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game of chance in which losers remove clothing until they are bare.

clue.text: "His —— were scarlet, but his books were read" (Belloc)

definitions.text: "His —— were scarlet, but his books were read" (Belloc)

parts.words: His —— were scarlet, but his books were read
parts.note: Belloc's epitaph on himself plays on Isaiah's scarlet wrongdoings and the pun read/red

explanation.surface: A quotation from Hilaire Belloc's mock epitaph.
explanation.walkthrough: Belloc wrote 'When I am dead, I hope it may be said: His sins were scarlet, but his books were read.' Isaiah 1:18 speaks of sins 'as scarlet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongdoings or transgressions, which Isaiah describes as scarlet.

clue.text: Insignia to be had for a sovereign

definitions.meaning: emblems such as crown and sceptre

definitions.text: to be had for a sovereign
definitions.meaning: things that belong to a monarch, read as though priced at a gold coin

explanation.surface: Royal emblems offered for sale at the price of a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is both a monarch and an old British gold pound coin, so the second half reads like a price tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal emblems of office, crown, orb and sceptre, are the trappings that belong to a monarch.

clue.text: Describing the Royal Society whose works are barred ?

definitions.text: Describing the Royal Society whose works are barred ?

parts.words: Describing the Royal Society whose works are barred
parts.note: musical compositions are written out in bars, and the Royal society in question devotes itself to orchestral music

explanation.surface: A learned body whose publications have been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Society is a science academy, the false trail; music is written in bars, so this is the Royal Philharmonic Society.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted to music, as in the name of orchestras and the Royal Philharmonic Society.

clue.text: Like 'those getting a penny for an hour's work, 'claimed others

definitions.text: Like 'those getting a penny for an hour's work, 'claimed others

parts.words: Like 'those getting a penny for an hour's work, 'claimed others
parts.note: the parable of the vineyard workers, where latecomers got the same penny as those who toiled all day, and the others complained

explanation.surface: Grumbling workers complain that some got a full penny for one hour.
explanation.walkthrough: In Matthew 20 every labourer is paid a penny (a denarius), and those who worked all day say the one-hour men got too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewarded with more money than the work deserves.

clue.text: Some ladies' crowning glory, indeed !

definitions.note: read as 'in deed': a deed held in trust by a third party

indicators.note: the word 'Some' tells us only part of the run of words is wanted

explanation.surface: An exclamation about women's hair as their crowning glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' is split as 'in deed': a document lodged with a third party until a condition is met.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond or document kept in trust by a third party until conditions are fulfilled, so held 'in deed'.

clue.text: Not many, we hear exclaim thus

indicators.note: the words 'we hear' tell the solver to go by how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: not many means few

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that there are not many, and hears an exclamation in reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of relief or exhaustion is the very word one would cry out, so it is the thing exclaimed.

clue.text: Happy days !

parts.note: calm, peaceful times of the past, after the kingfisher fabled to calm the seas

explanation.surface: A cheery toast or exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is 'halcyon days', from the halcyon bird said to calm the winter sea while nesting.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllically calm and happy, as in the idiom for a peaceful past period.

clue.text: Gained ground, contained communist rising, fabulous country

indicators.note: the word 'contained' tells us the two first pieces hold the communist inside

parts.note: won means gained
land is ground

indicators.note: in a down clue 'rising' means the communist is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: red is a communist

explanation.surface: A news report of territory gained and a communist uprising contained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns RED into DER, which sits between WON and LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's dream realm of Alice is a fabled, magical land.

clue.text: Carelessness, putting letters for North Carolina in a loose wrapper

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us the state's letters go inside the garment

parts.note: a negligee is a light loose dressing gown
NC is the postal abbreviation for the US state of North Carolina

explanation.surface: Instructions for addressing a parcel to North Carolina inside a flimsy wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The NC goes in between the last two letters of the gown, NEGLIGE + NC + E.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect of due care is a synonym for carelessness.

clue.text: It' would include Jock's sisters and his cousins and his' aunts

definitions.text: It' would include Jock's sisters and his cousins and his' aunts

parts.words: It' would include Jock's sisters and his cousins and his' aunts
parts.note: a Scotsman's whole extended family, borrowing a line from Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore, makes up his Highland kin group

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan line about a crowd of female relatives, applied to a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His sisters and his cousins and his aunts' is a famous line from HMS Pinafore; Jock is the stock name for a Scotsman, whose family group is a Scottish clan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish family group of related households sharing a surname and chief.

clue.text: William I's record sounds somewhat eschatological

indicators.note: the word 'sounds' tells us to go by pronunciation

parts.note: eschatology concerns the Last Judgment, Doomsday, so a book of Doomsday is somewhat eschatological

explanation.surface: A medieval register whose name has a ring of the end of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: William the Conqueror's 1086 survey is pronounced 'Doomsday', the Day of Judgment that eschatology studies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norman survey of English landholdings ordered by the Conqueror in 1086.

clue.text: The flower of Xanadu

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, and Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan names the sacred river running through Xanadu

explanation.surface: A botanist's question about what bloom grew in Kubla Khan's pleasure garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as 'flow-er', a crossword river; Coleridge's Kubla Khan opens 'In Xanadu did Kubla Khan... Where Alph, the sacred river, ran'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem names this as the sacred river that runs through Kubla Khan's domain.

clue.text: Pattern expert to be key operator ?

parts.note: a pro is an expert or professional
to type is to work the keys of a typewriter

explanation.surface: An expert at patterns wondering whether to become a keyboard operator.
explanation.definitionFit: An original model from which copies are made is a pattern.

clue.text: On the hot line ?

parts.note: the line here is the imaginary circle around the globe's middle, where the climate is hot

explanation.surface: Someone waiting on an emergency telephone link.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hot line' is a direct emergency phone link, the false trail; here it is the Earth's hottest latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying at or near the great circle of zero latitude, the tropics' hot middle.

clue.text: As such, rail transport has four lines

parts.note: qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', as such
a train is transport by rail

explanation.surface: A remark that a railway network, as such, runs four lines.
explanation.walkthrough: QUA, from Latin, means 'as' or 'in the capacity of'. 'Four lines' looks like railway tracks but is a stanza.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza or poem of exactly four lines of verse.

clue.text: Nuclear commanding officer, say?

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective while the answer is a noun: the central, nuclear part of a thing

indicators.note: the word 'say' signals that the officer's title is to be pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a colonel commands a regiment

explanation.surface: A military commander in charge of nuclear weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel is pronounced like 'kernel', the nucleus of a nut or seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or central part of something is its nucleus, so the word stands for what is nuclear.

clue.text: Ma takes nap later — a change from this duty?

definitions.text: Ma takes nap later — a change from this duty?

indicators.note: a change signals the letters of the two words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother sleeping later for once, a break from her usual chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A change' rearranges NAP LATER; the whole clue pictures a mother's break from her duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a mother or father, as with the obligations of raising children.

clue.text: It's curtains for him 'when his work's a success

definitions.text: It's curtains for him 'when his work's a success

parts.words: It's curtains for him 'when his work's a success
parts.note: when a play is a hit, the audience calls the writer onto the stage at the curtain call

explanation.surface: Someone whose success spells their doom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's curtains' usually means the end; here it is the curtain call, when a theatre audience shouts for the playwright to take a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of a play is called to the stage when it succeeds.

clue.text: "I swung the earth a —— at my wrist" (Thompson)

definitions.text: "I swung the earth a —— at my wrist" (Thompson)

parts.words: I swung the earth a —— at my wrist
parts.note: Francis Thompson's line pictures the world dangling as a small ornament on a bracelet

explanation.surface: A quotation from the poet Francis Thompson.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Francis Thompson's The Hound of Heaven: 'I swung the earth a trinket at my wrist'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cheap ornament, such as a charm hanging from a bracelet.

clue.text: A convenient chap for odd jobs

definitions.text: A convenient chap for odd jobs

parts.note: handy means convenient
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A useful fellow to call when small repairs need doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to do small repairs and odd jobs around a house.

clue.text: Cocktail needs skill in some fashion

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us the skill is placed inside the fashion

parts.note: the mini, the short skirt, was a fashion
art is skill

explanation.surface: Advice that mixing a cocktail takes some stylish skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin and vermouth drink is a classic mixed drink.

clue.text: What's left of this fruit to cause the fall of man ?

definitions.text: What's left of this fruit to cause the fall of man ?

parts.words: What's left of this fruit to cause the fall of man
parts.note: the discarded peel of a yellow fruit is the classic slipping hazard, recalling the apple of Eden

explanation.surface: A theological question about the forbidden fruit in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall of man' suggests Eden's apple; here the skin of this fruit makes a man slip and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A long curved yellow tropical fruit whose peel is proverbially slippery.

clue.text: Talk about one drink to start

indicators.note: the word 'about' means the talk goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to orate is to talk formally
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone discussing a single drink to begin the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into being or begin is to start.

clue.text: Investigators bring the cart back

indicators.note: the word 'back' tells us the cart is read in reverse

parts.note: a dray is a low heavy cart

explanation.surface: Detectives told to bring a cart back.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, is often called simply 'the Yard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland Yard stands for London's Metropolitan Police detectives.

clue.text: Something wrong with the lid, opening yesterday with difficulty

indicators.note: with difficulty signals that those letters are struggled into a new order
the opening of the word means its first part, here the first four letters

explanation.surface: Someone who could barely open their eye yesterday because of a sore eyelid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' takes YEST, the start of 'yesterday', and 'with difficulty' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the edge of an eyelid.

clue.text: It's dark in Kentucky

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A remark on how dark it is in Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Black as ink describes something very dark.

clue.text: He gets actors into: trouble with his drawings

definitions.text: He gets actors into: trouble with his drawings

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An artist whose caricatures land performers in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' rearranges ACTORS INTO; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist of satirical drawings can embarrass the actors he depicts.

clue.text: French author first to be sold?

parts.note: a lot is an item to be sold at auction
I is the Roman numeral one, as in 'Lot I'

explanation.surface: Asking which French writer goes under the hammer first.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre Loti was a French novelist; 'lot I' is the first lot offered in a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Loti was the pen name of a French naval officer and novelist.

clue.text: Cutter put on board

indicators.note: put on in an across clue means the cutter goes after the board

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging
a knife is a cutter

explanation.surface: A blade laid out on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' is an old word for a dining table, as in 'bed and board'.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife laid at a place setting for eating.
